mock_data.title: New Research on Computer Games
mock_data.passage:
A Japanese professor has produced evidence to show that computer games can have a bad effect on children. Many parents and grandparents have been saying this for years, but they were largely ignored, being regarded as technophobes.

Parental worries about computer games often relate to their effect on their children's health and on their social skills. They feel that they should be outside getting exercise and enjoying the fresh air while playing with their friends. Since many of them usually play by themselves, they live rather isolated lives, with little opportunity to interact with other people. As a result, they may be very poor at communication.

Parents are also worried in case the violence of many of the games will cause their children to become more aggressive and violent themselves. This anxiety also applies to television, which often shows scenes of extreme brutality.

There are fears, too, that the popularity of computer games has added to the dumbing down of the information and material used by today's generation. Because children often choose to play computer games instead of reading or doing their homework, the games are thought to have a bad effect on their education. Parents are also worried that video games will prevent their children from developing their creativity, if they spend all their time in front of a screen instead of drawing, writing stories, and so forth.

Professor Ryuta Kawashima of Tohoku University shares parental concerns about the bad effects of computer games, but for different, and considerably more scientific, reasons. Using state-of-the-art technology, he has conducted research which, he believes, shows that computer games may stunt the development of children's brains.

He has been able to show, by means of brain scans, that playing computer games stimulates activity in only part of the players' brains, the part associated with vision and movement. The frontal lobes of their brains, associated with learning, memory, emotion and self-control, are remaining underdeveloped.

If the children's ability to control their behaviour is being underdeveloped, then they are more likely to become violent. Unfortunately, Professor Kawashima's research appears to indicate that parental fears about computer games are justified.
mock_data.passageB1:
A professor in Japan has found evidence that computer games can be bad for children. Many parents and grandparents have said this for a long time. But people often didn't listen to them because they thought they didn't understand technology.

Parents often worry about how computer games affect their children's health and social skills. They think children should play outside, get exercise, and have fun with friends. But many children play games alone. This means they don't interact with other people very much. As a result, they might not be good at talking to others and communicating their needs.

Parents are also concerned that the violent games might make their children more aggressive. They also worry about violence on TV. Some parents think that computer games are making young people less intelligent. They believe that children play games instead of reading or doing homework. So, the games can have a bad effect on their learning and education.

Parents are also worried that computer games stop children from using their imagination. They spend too much time looking at a screen instead of drawing or writing stories. Professor Ryuta Kawashima from Tohoku University also thinks computer games are bad, but for scientific reasons.

He used new technology to do research. He thinks his research shows that computer games can stop children's brains from growing properly. He used brain scans to show that playing computer games only makes some parts of the brain active. These parts control seeing and moving. The parts of the brain that help with learning, memory, emotions, and self-control don't grow as much.

If children can't control their behaviour very well, they might become violent. It seems that Professor Kawashima's research shows that parents are right to be worried about computer games. Parents should pay attention to the time their children spend playing video games and encourage other activities.
mock_data.passageB2:
A recent study by a Japanese professor has unearthed evidence suggesting that computer games might negatively impact children. While many parents and grandparents have voiced similar concerns for years, they've often been dismissed as technologically resistant. These worries often revolve around the potential effects on children's physical health and social development.

Parents often feel that children should be outdoors, exercising and socialising with friends. Instead, many children play alone, leading to social isolation and limited opportunities for interaction, which can hinder their communication skills. There's also the concern that the violent content in many games could desensitise children to violence and potentially lead to more aggressive behaviour, a fear also associated with exposure to violent content on television.

Moreover, some worry that the pervasiveness of computer games contributes to a general decline in the complexity and depth of information that young people engage with. Because children may choose gaming over reading or homework, these games are thought to impede their academic progress. Parents are also concerned that excessive screen time might stifle creativity, preventing children from engaging in activities like drawing or writing.

Professor Ryuta Kawashima from Tohoku University shares these concerns about the potential adverse effects of computer games, but his research offers a more scientific perspective. Using advanced technology, his research aims to demonstrate that computer games may impair brain development in children.

His brain scans indicate that gaming primarily stimulates areas of the brain related to vision and movement. Crucially, the frontal lobes, which are instrumental in learning, memory, emotional regulation, and self-control, show signs of underdevelopment. If children's ability to control their behaviour is indeed being compromised, they might be more prone to aggressive outbursts. Professor Kawashima’s research seems to substantiate parental fears about the potential downsides of computer games.
mock_data.passageC1:
For years, anxieties surrounding the potential deleterious effects of computer games on children have been largely dismissed as the knee-jerk reactions of a generation unfamiliar with technology. However, a recent study conducted by a Japanese professor lends credence to these long-held concerns. The unease expressed by parents and grandparents often revolves around two key areas: the potential detriment to children's physical and social well-being. There's a prevailing sentiment that children should be outdoors, engaging in physical activity and cultivating interpersonal relationships, rather than leading increasingly isolated lives glued to screens. This sedentary lifestyle, coupled with limited face-to-face interaction, may impede the development of crucial communication skills.

Moreover, apprehensions persist regarding the desensitizing effect of violent video games, with parents fearing that exposure to such content may incline children towards aggressive behaviour. This concern mirrors anxieties surrounding the depiction of brutality on television. Furthermore, some commentators argue that the pervasive popularity of computer games has contributed to a dumbing down of educational content. The perceived trade-off between screen time and academic pursuits, such as reading and homework, has fueled anxieties about the negative impact on children's intellectual development. The concern also extends to the potential stifling of creativity, with parents fearing that excessive screen time may preclude children from engaging in activities that foster imagination, such as drawing or creative writing.

Professor Ryuta Kawashima of Tohoku University, however, approaches these concerns from a distinctly scientific perspective. His research, utilizing cutting-edge neuroimaging technology, suggests that computer games may indeed impair the holistic development of children's brains. Specifically, brain scans have revealed that gaming primarily stimulates the areas associated with visual processing and motor control, while the frontal lobes – responsible for higher-order cognitive functions such as learning, memory, emotional regulation, and self-control – remain relatively dormant. This selective stimulation raises concerns about potential imbalances in brain development.

The implications of underdeveloped frontal lobes are far-reaching, particularly in relation to behavioural control. If the capacity for self-regulation is compromised, children may be more susceptible to impulsive and potentially aggressive behaviour. Professor Kawashima's findings, therefore, appear to corroborate parental anxieties, suggesting that the potential negative consequences of excessive computer game usage may be more profound than previously acknowledged. Further research is undoubtedly needed to fully elucidate the complex interplay between gaming and child development and to devise strategies for mitigating potential harm, but this study serves as a wake-up call for parents and educators alike.

mock_data.translation:
Yaponiyalik professor kompyuter o'yinlarining bolalarga yomon ta'sir qilishi mumkinligini ko'rsatuvchi dalillarni taqdim etdi. Ko'pgina ota-onalar va bobo-buvilar buni yillar davomida aytib kelishmoqda, ammo ular asosan texnofoblar (technophobes - texnologiyadan qo'rquvchilar) deb hisoblanib, e'tiborsiz qoldirilgan.

Kompyuter o'yinlari haqidagi ota-onalarning xavotirlari ko'pincha ularning farzandlari sog'lig'iga va ijtimoiy ko'nikmalariga (social skills) ta'siri bilan bog'liq. Ular bolalar tashqarida mashq qilishlari, do'stlari bilan o'ynab toza havoda zavqlanishlari kerak deb hisoblashadi. Ularning ko'pchiligi odatda o'zlari o'ynaganlari sababli, boshqa odamlar bilan muloqot qilish (interact) imkoniyati kam bo'lgan juda yakkalangan (isolated) hayot kechirishadi. Natijada, ular muloqotda (communication) juda zaif bo'lib qolishlari mumkin.

Ota-onalar, shuningdek, ko'plab o'yinlardagi zo'ravonlik ularning farzandlarini yanada tajovuzkor (aggressive) va zo'ravon bo'lib qolishiga sabab bo'lishidan xavotirda. Ushbu xavotir ko'pincha haddan tashqari shafqatsizlik (brutality) sahnalarini ko'rsatadigan televideniyega ham tegishli.

Kompyuter o'yinlarining ommaviyligi bugungi avlod tomonidan foydalaniladigan ma'lumot va materiallarning saviyasini pasaytirib yuborayotganidan (dumbing down) ham qo'rqishadi. Bolalar ko'pincha kitob o'qish yoki uy vazifalarini bajarish o'rniga kompyuter o'yinlarini o'ynashni tanlaganlari sababli, o'yinlar ularning ta'limiga yomon ta'sir ko'rsatadi deb hisoblanadi. Ota-onalar, shuningdek, agar bolalar rasm chizish, hikoya yozish va hokazolar o'rniga barcha vaqtlarini ekran qarshisida o'tkazsalar, video o'yinlar (video games) ularning ijodkorligini (creativity) rivojlanishiga to'sqinlik qilishidan xavotirda.

Tohoku universitetining professori Ryuta Kavashima kompyuter o'yinlarining yomon ta'siri haqidagi ota-onalarning xavotirlarini qo'llab-quvvatlaydi, ammo boshqa va ancha ilmiyroq sabablarga ko'ra. Zamonaviy (state-of-the-art) texnologiyalardan foydalangan holda, u kompyuter o'yinlari bolalar miyasining rivojlanishini to'xtatib qo'yishi (stunt) mumkinligini ko'rsatadigan tadqiqot o'tkazdi.

U miyani skanerlash orqali kompyuter o'yinlarini o'ynash o'yinchilar miyasining faqat bir qismini, ya'ni ko'rish (vision) va harakat (movement) bilan bog'liq qismini rag'batlantirishini (stimulates) ko'rsata oldi. Miyaning o'rganish, xotira, hissiyot (emotion) va o'zini nazorat qilish bilan bog'liq bo'lgan peshona bo'laklari (frontal lobes) rivojlanmagan holda qolmoqda.

Agar bolalarning o'z xulq-atvorini nazorat qilish qobiliyati rivojlanmagan bo'lsa, u holda ular zo'ravonlikka moyil bo'lishlari ehtimoli ko'proq. Afsuski, professor Kavashimaning tadqiqoti kompyuter o'yinlari haqidagi ota-onalarning xavotirlari o'rinli ekanligini (justified) ko'rsatmoqda.

mock_data.translationB1:
Yaponiyalik professor kompyuter o'yinlari bolalar uchun yomon bo'lishi mumkinligi haqida dalillar topdi. Ko'plab ota-onalar va buvi-buvalar buni uzoq vaqtdan beri aytib kelishgan. Ammo odamlar ko'pincha ularga quloq solishmadi, chunki ular texnologiyani tushunmaydi deb o'ylashdi.

Ota-onalar ko'pincha kompyuter o'yinlari bolalar salomatligiga va ijtimoiy ko'nikmalariga qanday ta'sir qilishi haqida xavotirlanishadi. Ular bolalar tashqarida o'ynashi, jismoniy mashqlar qilishi va do'stlari bilan vaqt o'tkazishi kerak deb o'ylashadi. Ammo ko'plab bolalar yolg'iz o'yin o'ynashadi. Bu ularning boshqa odamlar bilan unchalik muloqot qilmasligini anglatadi. Natijada, ular boshqalar bilan gaplasha olmasligi va o'z ehtiyojlarini ifoda eta olmasligi mumkin.

Ota-onalar, shuningdek, zo'ravonlik o'yinlari bolalarini yanada tajovuzkor qilib qo'yishidan xavotirda. Ular televizordagi zo'ravonlik haqida ham xavotirlanishadi. Ba'zi ota-onalar kompyuter o'yinlari yoshlarni kamroq aqlli qilib qo'yapti deb o'ylashadi. Ular bolalar kitob o'qish yoki uy vazifasini bajarish o'rniga o'yin o'ynaydi deb hisoblashadi.
